chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said:

Talha ibn Ubaydillah entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and in the hand of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was a quince which had been brought to him; and he said: 'Take it, O Aba Muhammad, for indeed it will relieve the heart.'

key_terms.أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, a kunya (honorific) used for Talha
key_terms.طَلْحَةُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ: Talha ibn Ubaydillah, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the quince given by the Prophet to Talha in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) use of quince as a therapeutic remedy for calming the heart, reflecting the broader Islamic tradition of utilizing natural elements for physical and spiritual well-being. It underscores the practical wisdom embedded in prophetic gifts, where simple items like fruit serve both medicinal purposes and as symbols of care and benevolence.
